name: Kingdom of Reman
description: The state of Reman was founded in 1810 in Patani (today Thailand) between the older principalities of Pujut, Jalor and Legeh.

name: Kingdom of Rheged
label: celtic polities in britain;celtic polities
description: Was a Brittonic kingdom in what are now Northern England and southern Scotland, during the post-Roman era and Early Middle Ages.

name: Kingdom of Rimatara
description: Was the precolonial kingdom that occupied the island of the same name in French Polynesia. In 1889 it became a French Protectorate.

name: Kingdom of Rimatara (France)
description: Was the precolonial kingdom that occupied the island of the same name in French Polynesia. In 1889 it became a French Protectorate.

name: Cuzcatlecs
label: mesoamerican polities
description: Was a pre-Columbian Nahua state confederation of the Mesoamerican postclassical period that extended from the Paz river to the Lempa river (covering most of western El Salvador).

name: Kingdom of Romania
description: The Kingdom of Romania succeeded the Romanian United Principalities in 1881 with the crowning of prince Karl of Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen as King Carol I.

name: Kingdom of Rome
description: According to oral accounts, the Roman Kingdom began with the city's founding c. 753 BC. It was the earliest form of the Roman state. During this period Rome controlled just the territory around the city.

name: Kingdom of Rujumbura
label: african great lakes kingdoms
description: Was one of the precolonial African Great Lakes Kingdoms.

name: Kingdom of Rurutu
description: Was the precolonial kingdom that occupied the island of the same name in French Polynesia. In 1889 it became a French Protectorate and in 1900 it was annexed to the French Establishments in Oceania.

name: Kingdom of Rurutu (France)
description: Was the precolonial kingdom that occupied the island of the same name in French Polynesia. In 1889 it became a French Protectorate and in 1900 it was annexed to the French Establishments in Oceania.

name: Dachange
description: Was the polity that ruled over Nanzhao after Zheng Maisi overthrew the ruling dynasty. It was centered on present-day Yunnan in China.

name: Daju kingdom
description: Was a medieval monarchy that existed in Darfur (Sudan) from possibly the 12th-15th century.

name: Dali Kingdom
description: Was the polity that ruled over Nanzhao after Duan Siping overthrew the ruling dynasty. It was centered on present-day Yunnan in China.

name: Kingdom of Rwanda
description: The Kingdom of Rwanda was a precolonial kingdom in East Africa. It was later colonized first by the Germans, and after World War I by the Belgians. It gained independence from Belgium in 1959 but was replaced by a Republican system shortly after.

name: Kingdom of Saloum
description: Was a Serer/Wolof kingdom in present-day Senegal and Gambia.

name: Kingdom of Sam'al
label: luwian-aramean polities;aramean polities
description: Was a Syro-Hittite state (Luwian-, Aramaic- and Phoenician-speaking political entities in northern Syria and southern Anatolia that emerged after the collapse of the Hittite Empire).

name: Danelaw
label: norse/viking polities
description: Was the part of England conquered by Norsemen from 865. Viking rule ended when Eric Bloodaxe was driven out of Northumbria in 954.

name: Kingdom of Sanwi (France)
description: Was a precolonial Kingdom established in about 1740 by Anyi migrants from Ghana in modern-day Ivory Coast. In 1843 the kingdom became a protectorate of France.

name: Danta State
description: Was a polity in modern-day Gujarat, in India.

name: Daspalla State
description: Was a polity located in the modern-day Indian State of Odisha.

name: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
description: Is a country that covers most of the Arabian Peninsula. It is ruled by the House of Saud, that created several polities in the region since 1745. Modern Saudi Arabia originated from the the legal merger of Nejd and Hejaz in 1932.

name: Datarpur State
description: A small precolonial Indian hill state in the Lower Himalayas.

name: Datia State
description: Was a polity located in the modern-day Indian State of Madhya Pradesh.

name: Kingdom of Seisyllwg
label: celtic polities in britain;welsh polities;celtic polities
description: Was one of several Welsh kingdoms that emerged in 5th-century post-Roman Britain.

name: Kingdom of Serbia
description: In 1882 the Principality of Serbia was elevated to the status of kingdom. Between 1912 and 1913, Serbia greatly enlarged its territory through engagement in the First and Second Balkan Wars. After World War I it merged with nearby territories to form the Kingdom of the Slovenes, Croats and Serbs.

name: Datianxing
description: Was the polity that ruled over Nanzhao after Zhao Shanzheng overthrew the ruling dynasty. It was centered on present-day Yunnan in China.

name: Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes
description: Was a state in Southeast and Central Europe that was established when Serbia united with the newly created State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs. The official name of the state was changed to "Kingdom of Yugoslavia" by King Alexander I on 3 October 1929.

name: Kingdom of Setul Mambang Segara
description: Was a Malay kingdom founded in the northern coast of the Malay Peninsula. The state was established in 1808 in wake of the partition between the rulers in the royal house of Kedah.

name: Kingdom of Shewa
description: Was a kingdom in Ethiopia.

name: Kingdom of Shupria
description: Was a kingdom in the Armenian highlands known from Assyrian sources.

name: Kingdom of Siang
description: Was one of the precolonial polities that existed on the island of Sulawesi (Indonesia).

name: Kingdom of Sicily
label: norse/viking polities;norman polities in southern italy
description: Was a Kingdom that emerged from the union of the county of Sicily (that controlled Sicily and Malta) with the Norman possessions in southern Italy (that included the entire southern Italian Peninsula south to the Papal States, the same region of the later Kingdom of Naples). In 1282 a revolt against the Angevin rule (the Sicilian Vespers) divided the kingdom in two, the Kingdom of Sicily being reduced again to the sole island of the same name. After Sicily entered into a Personal Union with Aragon in 1479, the Kingdom was always controlled by an external country. It ceased to exist in 1816 when it was merged with the Kingdom of Naples to form the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.

name: Dayining
description: Was the polity that ruled over Nanzhao after Yang Ganzhen overthrew the ruling dynasty. It was centered on present-day Yunnan in China.

name: Dazhong Kingdom
description: Was the polity that ruled over Nanzhao for a short period after Gao Shengtai overthrew the ruling dynasty. It was centered on present-day Yunnan in China.

name: North Sea Empire (Denmark-England)
label: norse/viking polities
description: Was the Personal Union of the Kingdoms of Denmark and England.

name: Denmark-Norway
description: Was the union of Denmark and Norway. It was formed several times between 1001 and 1814.

name: North Sea Empire (Denmark-Norway-England)
label: norse/viking polities
description: Was the Personal Union of the Kingdoms of Denmark, Norway and England.

name: Despotate of Angelokastron and Lepanto
label: albanian principalities
description: Created after the defeat of Nikephoros II Orsini in 1358 in Western Greece.

name: Kingdom of Sigave
description: Was a precolonial kingdom on the island of the same name in the South Pacific Ocean. In 1887 it became a French Protectorate and was later inglobated into the colony of Wallis and Futuna.

name: Kingdom of Sigave (France)
description: Was a precolonial kingdom on the island of the same name in the South Pacific Ocean. In 1887 it became a French Protectorate and was later inglobated into the colony of Wallis and Futuna.

name: Kingdom of Sikkim
description: The Kingdom of Sikkim was a hereditary monarchy in the Eastern Himalayas. It was ruled by Chogyals of the Namgyal dynasty. It became a British Protectorate in 1861. It gained independency in 1947, but became an Indian protectorate shortly after and was finally inglobated into India.

name: Kingdom of Sikkim (Great Britain)
description: The Kingdom of Sikkim was a hereditary monarchy in the Eastern Himalayas. With the Treaty of Tumlong of 1861, Sikkim became a British Protectroate.

name: Kingdom of Sikkim (India)
description: The Kingdom of Sikkim was a hereditary monarchy in the Eastern Himalayas. It was ruled by Chogyals of the Namgyal dynasty. It became a British Protectorate in 1861. It gained independency in 1947, but became an Indian protectorate shortly after and was finally inglobated into India.

name: Despotate of Arta
label: albanian principalities
description: A despotate established by Albanian rulers during the 14th century, after the defeat of the local Despot of Epirus, Nikephoros II Orsini, by Albanian tribesmen in the Battle of Achelous in 1359.

name: Despotate of Dobruja
description: Split off from the Second Bulgarian Empire under the influence of the Byzantine Empire. It controlled modern Dobruja.

name: Kingdom of Sitawaka
description: Was a Kingdom in Sri Lanka that emerged from the division of Kotte in 1521. The Kingdom was conquered by the Portuguese in 1593.

name: Teutonic Order in Transylvania
label: states emerged from the northern crusades
description: The Teutonic Order was created in the Kingdom of Jerusalem but after the defeat of the Christian forces in the Middle East, it moved to Transylvania to help the Kingdom of Hungary against the Cumans. Here the Order created a factually independent domain until they were expelled by King Andre II of Hungary in 1225.

name: Kingdom of Soissons (Chilperic I)
label: barbarian kingdoms;frankish polities
description: Was one of the many Frankish Teilreiche (polities emerging from the hereditary divisions of the Frankish Kingdom that repeatedly divided and reunited) of the Merovingian Dynasty. It originated with the division of the Empire at the death of King Chlothar I.

name: Kingdom of Solimana
description: Solimana was a minor West African state of the nineteenth century with a capital at the fortress town of Falaba (Sierra Leone).

name: Kingdom of Soukouma
label: african great lakes kingdoms
description: Was one of the precolonial African Great Lakes Kingdoms.

name: Kingdom of Spain
description: Is a country that occupies most of the Iberian Peninsula. The country emerged in 1469,  when the crowns of the Christian kingdoms of Castile and Aragon were united by the marriage of their monarchs. The two Kingdoms remained legally separated, but from this moment factually acted as one country. The two Kingdoms were legally merged by Philip V in 1715 (Nueva Planta decrees). The modern Kingdom of Spain succeeded the Spanish State, an autoritarian regime, in 1975.

name: Deva dynasty
description: The dynasty ruled over eastern Bengal after the Sena dynasty.

name: Dewas State
description: Was a polity located in the modern-day Indian State of Madhya Pradesh. The separation of the polity in a Junior and Senior Line is not considered in this model.

name: Dhar State
description: Was an Indian polity whose core lied in the city of Dhar, in modern-day Madhya Pradesh.

name: Kingdom of Strathclyde
label: celtic polities in britain;celtic polities
description: Strathclyde was one of the early medieval kingdoms of the Britons that emerged after the end of Roman Rule in Britain. It comprised the Brythonic-speaking parts of what is now southern Scotland and northern England.

name: Kingdom of Sumer
description: Lugal-Zage-Si of Umma united Sumer (southern modern-day Iraq) briefly into a single kingdom.

name: Kingdom of Sussex
label: saxon polities in britain
description: Was an early medieval kingdom in what is now South England, one of the polities founded by the Saxons in Post-Roman Britain. It existed from either the fifth or the sixth century CE. After intermittent periods of domains by Mercia and Wessex, it was finally absorbed by the latter.

name: Kingdom of Sussex (Mercia)
label: saxon polities in britain
description: Was an early medieval kingdom in what is now South England, one of the polities founded by the Saxons in Post-Roman Britain. It existed from either the fifth or the sixth century CE. After intermittent periods of domains by Mercia and Wessex, it was finally absorbed by the latter.

name: Kingdom of Sussex (Wessex)
label: saxon polities in britain
description: Was an early medieval kingdom in what is now South England, one of the polities founded by the Saxons in Post-Roman Britain. It existed from either the fifth or the sixth century CE. After intermittent periods of domains by Mercia and Wessex, it was finally absorbed by the latter.

name: Kingdom of Swaziland
description: The Swazi settled in present-day Eswatini around 1745. After the Second Boer War the Kingdom became a British protectorate which lasted until 1968.

name: Kingdom of Sweden
description: Is a Nordic country located on the Scandinavian Peninsula in Northern Europe. Sweden exists as a country since 970 AD. King Sverker I of Sweden (1134-55) is said to have permanently integrated Götaland and Svealand into the Kingdom of Sweden.

name: Dharampur State
description: Was an Indian polity located in the modern-day Indian State of Gujarat.

name: Dharmasraya
description: A Buddhist polity that ruled over the western portion of the island of Sumatra.

name: Dhaulpur State
description: Was a polity located in the modern-day Indian State of Rajasthan.

name: Dhenkanal State
description: Was a polity located in the modern-day Indian State of Odisha.

name: Dhrangadhra State
description: Was an Indian polity located in the modern-day Indian State of Gujarat.

name: Dhrol State
description: Was an Indian polity located in the modern-day Indian State of Gujarat.

name: Dhundhar State
description: Jaipur's predecessor state was the kingdom of Dhundhar or Dausa, founded in 1093 by Dullah Rai, also known as Dulha Rao.

name: Dhurwai State
description: Was a polity located in the modern-day Indian State of Uttar Pradesh.

name: Kingdom of Taiohae (France)
description: Was a precolonial kingdom in the Marquesas Islands that ruled over the island with the same name. It became a French Protectorate in 1842.

name: Kingdom of Tallo
description: Was one of the precolonial polities that existed on the island of Sulawesi (Indonesia).

name: Kingdom of Tambapanni
description: Was the first Sinhalese kingdom in Sri Lanka. Its administrative centre was based at Tambapaṇṇī, in the north of the island.

name: Dimasa Kingdom
description: Was a late medieval/early modern kingdom in Assam, Northeast India ruled by Dimasa kings.

name: Đinh dynasty
description: Was a Dynasty that succeeded to the Ngô Dynasty.

name: Kingdom of Tawana
description: Was a precolonial kingdom in Botswana.

name: Kingdom of Taytay
label: barangay states
description: Was precolonial polity in the Philippines.

name: Kingdom of Thailand
description: Is a country in Southeast Asia, located at the centre of the Indochinese Peninsula. Siam exist as a country since the Ayutthaya Kingdom (1351-1767). The modern Kingdom of Thailand  was established after the Siamese revolution of 1932.

name: Kingdom of the Alans in Spain
label: barbarian kingdoms;frankish polities
description: Was one of the many kingdoms created by Germanic peoples during the Migration Period.

name: Kingdom of the Alemanni
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: Romans controlled the Agri Decumates (southwestern Germany) region until the mid-3rd century, when the emperor Gallienus (259-260) evacuated it before the invading Alemanni, a Germanic Tribe, that esablished their Kingdom in the region.

name: Kingdom of the Alemanni (Frankish)
label: barbarian kingdoms;frankish polities
description: Was the kingdom of the Germanic Tribe of the Alemanni in southwestern Germany. The Kingdom was a Frankish Vassal since the military expedition of Clovis in 496.

name: Kingdom of the Aures
label: roman-maurian kingdoms;berber kingdoms
description: Was an independent Christian Berber kingdom primarily located in the Aurès Mountains of present-day north-eastern Algeria.

name: Kingdom of the Bavarians
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: The Bavarians were a Germanic Tribe that created a Kingdom in the modern-day German State that takes its name from them. They were first mentioned in chronicles between 520 and 551. The Bavarians probably invaded the region of Bavaria during the time of the Gothic-Byzantine wars.

name: Kingdom of the Burgundians
description: During the decline of the Western Roman Empire, the Germanic Tribe of the Burgundians settled in central and southern France, as well as western Switzerland. Initially foederati (bound by a treaty) of the Romans, with the Falls of the Western Roman Empire the Kingdom became completely independent. The modern region of Burgundy in Europe derives its name from the Tribe.

name: Kingdom of the Burgundians (Foederati)
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: During the decline of the Western Roman Empire, the Germanic Tribe of the Burgundians settled in central and southern France, as well as western Switzerland. Initially foederati (bound by a treaty) of the Romans, with the Fall of the Western Roman Empire the Kingdom became completely independent. The modern region of Burgundy in Europe derives its name from the Tribe.

name: Kingdom of the Burgundians in Rhineland
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: The Germanic Tribe of the Burgundians settled in the Rhineland and were made Roman foederati (a territory bound to the Roman Empire by a treaty). It was a different polity than the Burgundian Kingdom in southern France.

name: Kingdom of the Dorsale
label: roman-maurian kingdoms;berber kingdoms
description: Was one of the many petty kingdoms that emerged from the collapse of the Mauro-Roman Kingdom.

name: Kingdom of the Franks
label: barbarian kingdoms;frankish polities
description: Was the Kingdom of the Franks, a Germanic Tribe. Their Kingdom was founded during the period of fragementation of the Western Roman Empire. The initial core of their Kingdom was located in Northern France and Belgium. The Kingdom of the Franks was partitioned and reunited several times as the Frankish rulers usually divided their territories among their heirs. In the year 800 Charlemagne was crowned in Rome and the Kingdom became an Empire.

name: Kingdom of the Garamantes
description: The Garamantes emerged as a major regional power in the mid second century AD, establishing a kingdom in Libya.

name: Kingdom of the Gepids (First Kingdom)
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: The Gepids were an East germanic Tribe that initially settled in the Carpathian basin were they founded their first Kingdom around 350 AD.

name: Kingdom of the Gepids (Second Kingdom)
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: The Gepids were an East germanic Tribe. They created a second Kingdom in the Eastern Carpathian basin in 454 AD, during the Migration periods. The Gepid Kingdom was destroyed by the Avars and Lombards in 567.

name: Kingdom of the Heruls
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: Was one of the many kingdoms created by Germanic peoples during the Migration Period.

name: Kingdom of the Hodna
label: roman-maurian kingdoms;berber kingdoms
description: Was one of the many petty kingdoms that emerged from the collapse of the Mauro-Roman Kingdom.

name: Kingdom of the Hwicce
label: celtic polities in britain;celtic polities
description: Was a tribal kingdom in Anglo-Saxon England.

name: Domain of Braničevo
description: Darman and Kudelin were two Bulgarian nobles who jointly ruled the region of Braničevo (in modern Serbia) as independent or semi-independent autocrats in the late 13th century (1273-1291).

name: Domain of Branković
label: serbian principalities
description: One of the short lived semi-independent states that emerged from the collapse of the Serbian Empire in 1371, following the death of the last Emperor Uroš the Weak (1346-1371).

name: Kingdom of the Lombards
label: lombard polities;barbarian kingdoms
description: Was the kingdom of the Lombards, a Germanic people, during the Migration Period (also known as the Barbarian Invasions). The Lombards had initially established themselves in Noricum, modern-day eastern Austria, but left the region to settle in Italy, controlled by the Byzantine at the time. The Lombards quickly conquered most of Italy, with the exception of Latium and the Exarchate of Ravenna. The Kingdom was conquered by the Frankish Empire in 774. The Lombard domains in southern Italy were autonomous and lasted longer, being conquered by the Normans in the XI and XII centuries.

name: Kingdom of the Lombards in Noricum
label: lombard polities
description: Was the first kingdom of the Lombards, a Germanic people, during the Migration Period (also known as the Barbarian Invasions). It was located in Noricum, modern-day eastern Austria. The Lombards later left Noricum and estblished themselves in the Italian Peninsula.

name: Kingdom of the Maldives
description: The Kingdom of the Maldives, or Dheeva Mar, controlled the Maldivian Archipelago. It existed since 269 BC.

name: Kingdom of the Mannai
description: Was an ancient kingdom located in northwestern Iran, south of Lake Urmia.

name: Kingdom of the Mannai (Assyria)
description: Was an ancient kingdom located in northwestern Iran, south of Lake Urmia. It was a vassal of the Assyrian Empire from 717 BC.

name: Kingdom of the Nemencha
label: roman-maurian kingdoms;berber kingdoms
description: Was one of the many petty kingdoms that emerged from the collapse of the Mauro-Roman Kingdom.

name: Kingdom of the Netherlands
description: With the de facto secession of Belgium, the Netherlands was left as a rump state and refused to recognise Belgian independence until 1839 when the Treaty of London was signed, fixing the border between the two states and guaranteeing Belgian independence and neutrality as the Kingdom of Belgium.

name: Kingdom of the Ostrogoths
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: The Ostrogoths, officially Foederati of the Roman Empire, became factually independent when they moved into Pannonia. At the end of the V century AD they conquered Italy establishing a Kingdom there. In 553 AD the Italian Kingdom of the Ostrogoths was reconquered by the Eastern Roman Empire.

name: Kingdom of the Ostrogoths in Dacia
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: Was the first Kingdom founded by the Ostrogoths. It was located in Dacia (modern-day Romania) and lasted until its conquest by the Hunnic Empire.

name: Kingdom of the Ostrogoths in Moesia
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: In 382 AD the Thervingi and Gruthungi Ostrogoths became Foederati of the Roman Empire, and were allowed to establish a country in Moesia and Lower Scythia.

name: Kingdom of the Ourasenis
label: roman-maurian kingdoms;berber kingdoms
description: Was one of the many petty kingdoms that emerged from the collapse of the Mauro-Roman Kingdom.

name: Kingdom of the Picts
label: celtic polities in britain;celtic polities
description: Was the Kingdom of the Picts, a celtic population of Britain, that emerged after the Romans left Britain.

name: Kingdom of the Rugii
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: Was one of the many kingdoms created by Germanic peoples during the Migration Period.

name: Kingdom of the Scirii
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: Was one of the many kingdoms created by Germanic peoples during the Migration Period.

name: Kingdom of the Siraces
description: Was the kingdom of the Siraces, a Sarmatian population that inhabitated the Kuban region of Caucasus.

name: Kingdom of the Suebi in Galicia
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: In 409 AD The Vandals, Alans and Suebes invaded the Western Roman Empire and established themselves in the Iberian Peninsula. They created three separate kingdoms in the region. The Suebi, a Germanic people, occupied the region of Galicia. The Kingdom ceased to exist when it was conquered by the Visigoths in 585 AD.

name: Kingdom of the Suebi on the Danube
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: After the Battle of Nedao against the Huns in 454, the Suebi, a Germanic people, founded a small and short-lived kingdom in the old settlement area of the Marcomanni and the Quadi.

name: Domain of Jan Conny
description: Was the domain created by an indigenous Akan warrior centred on the abandonded  fort of Fredericksburg (that had been built by Brandenburg in modern-day Ghana).

name: Kingdom of the Tui Manuʻa
description: Was a a kingdom that ruled over the Manuʻa Islands in present-day American Samoa.

name: Domain of Hayreddin Barbarossa
description: In 1514 the Ottoman corsair Hayreddin Barbarossa captured Algiers from Spain.

name: Domain of Leo Gabalas
description: In the first half of the 13th century, Rhodes became the centre of an independent domain under Leo Gabalas and his brother John.

name: Kingdom of the Vandals
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: The Vandals left Spain in 429 and conquered most of the Roman territories in western north Africa. This was the sixth and final known kingdom founded by the Vandals. It ceased to exist when the Eastern Roman Empire managed to reconquer the region.

name: Kingdom of the Vandals Hasdingi in Spain
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: In 409 AD The Vandals, Alans and Suebes invaded the Western Roman Empire and established themselves in the Iberian Peninsula. They created three separate kingdoms in the region. The Vandals established themselves in Galicia, creating two kingdoms (on for the tribe of the Hasdingi and one for the tribe of the Silingi). Together, the two kingdoms are the third and fourth known kingdom created by the Vandals.

name: Kingdom of the Vandals in Betica
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: After a military intervention by the Romans, the Vandals left their territories and established a Kingdom in the Spanish region of Betica, the fifth known Vandal kingdom.

name: Kingdom of the Vandals in Dacia
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: During the the Marcomannic Wars the Vandals, a Germanic population, stipulated an alliance treaty with the Romans and established themselves in Dacia (modern-day Romania). It was the first known kingdom of the Vandals.

name: Kingdom of the Vandals in Pannonia
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: In 335 AD the Vandals established themselves in Pannonia as foederati of the empire after Constantine expelled them from Dacia. It was the second known kingdom of the Vandals.

name: Kingdom of the Vandals Silingi in Spain
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: In 409 AD The Vandals, Alans and Suebes invaded the Western Roman Empire and established themselves in the Iberian Peninsula. They created three separate kingdoms in the region. The Vandals established themselves in Galicia, creating two kingdoms (on for the tribe of the Hasdingi and one for the tribe of the Silingi). Together, the two kingdoms are the third and fourth known kingdom created by the Vandals.

name: Kingdom of the Visigoths
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: Was the Kingdom established by the Visigoths, a Germanic Tribe, in the Western Roman Empire territory during the late period of the Empire. Initially, it occupied Western Spain and Aquitaine. Soon it was able to conquer the Swabian Kingdom, that controleld the western Iberian Peninsula, but at the same time lost most of its territories in France to the Franks. The Kingdom of the Visigoths ceased to exist when the Iberian Pensinsula was conquered by the Caliphate of the Umayyads.

name: Kingdom of the Visigoths (Ostrogoths)
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: Was a short period of the Visigothic Empire were the polity was de facto controlled by Theodoric, King of the Ostrogoths, initiall through the puppet government of his grandson Amalaric (a child at the time).

name: Kingdom of Thessalonica
label: frankokratia
description: Was a short-lived Crusader State founded after the Fourth Crusade over conquered Byzantine lands in Macedonia and Thessaly.

name: Kingdom of Thessalonike
label: diadochi
description: Was one of the four Roman client republics into which Antigonid Macedonia was divided after the Third Macedonian War.

name: Domain of Teresa and Henry
description: A polity in Galicia that seceded during a civil war in the Kingdom of Leon.

name: Kingdom of Thuringia
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: Was the kingdom established by the Thuringians, a Germanic people, in eastern Germany during the great migration period.

name: Kingdom of Thuringia (Franks)
label: barbarian kingdoms
description: The Kingdom of the Thuringians was invaded and vassalized several times by the Franks until its final integration in the Frankish Empire in 843.

name: Kingdom of Timarchus
label: seleucid secessionist states
description: Timarchus was a usurper in the Seleucid empire between 163-160 BC. He controlled the Persian east of the Empire.

name: Domain of Thessaly
description: Was a polity that emerged from the division of the Despotate of Epirus.

name: Domain of Ugrin Csak
description: After the extinction of the Árpád dynasty in 1301, Ugrin Csak was among the so-called oligarchs or provincial lords, who ruled de facto independently their dominions. The domain was centered in the Syrmia region.

name: Dompu Kingdom
description: A polity on the island of Sumbawa, in the Sunda Islands (Indonesia).

name: Doura Kingdom
description: Was a precolonial kingdom in northern Nigeria.

name: Kingdom of Tonga
description: Is a Polynesian country and archipelago. The country has 171 islands. In the 10th century, the Tu'i Tonga Empire was established in the island of Tonga. In 1900 the Kingdom became a British protectorate and was added to the British Western Pacific Territories. It was a separate protectorate from 1953, until it re-emerged as an independent country in 1970.

name: Kingdom of Tooro
label: african great lakes kingdoms
description: Was one of the precolonial African Great Lakes Kingdoms.

name: Duchy of Bohemia
label: holy roman empire
description: Bohemia emerged as a duchy around 870 AD, the first form of the modern-day Czech State. It was a vassal of the Frankish Empire until 962 when East Francia became the Holy Roman Empire, of which Bohemia initially was not part of.

name: Duchy of Croatia
description: Was a medieval state that was established by White Croats who migrated into the area of the former Roman province of Dalmatia. It became a kingdom in 926. It was the first form of the Croatian state. It ended when it entered in Personal Union with Hungary, with the latter being the dominant part of the two (However, it is not completely clear how autonomous Croatia was in practice).

name: Duchy of Lithuania
description: Was a polity created by the Lithuanians in the 13th century. Initially a Duchy, it became Kingdom in 1251 when Duke Mindaugas converted to Christianity. However the rulers immediately after Mindaugas remained pagans and created the Grand Duchy of Lithuania. Lithuania grew to be a regional power, being able to defeat the Mongols and inglobate many of the small principalities that had succeeded the Kievan Rus'.
